data.name: Tech_T1078.004_Desc
data.value: Guest (external) identities and the groups that contain them provide an attacker-controllable entry vector into the tenant; guests inheriting group-based access widen the reachable resources from outside the organisation.

data.name: Tech_T1078.004_Mit
data.value: Govern guest lifecycle with access reviews and expiration; restrict guest permissions and remove guests from privileged or broadly-scoped groups; limit which groups may contain guests.

data.name: Tech_T1558.003_Desc
data.value: Adversaries request service tickets for accounts that expose a Service Principal Name and crack them offline to recover the account password.

data.name: Tech_T1558.003_Mit
data.value: Minimise user accounts carrying an SPN; use Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) and enforce long, complex passwords.

data.name: Tech_T1558.004_Desc
data.value: Accounts that do not require Kerberos pre-authentication allow an attacker to request encrypted material and crack it offline.

data.name: Tech_T1558.004_Mit
data.value: Require Kerberos pre-authentication on all accounts.

data.name: Tech_T1555_Desc
data.value: Reversible encryption and DES encryption store or transmit passwords in a recoverable/weak form, easing credential recovery.

data.name: Tech_T1555_Mit
data.value: Disable reversible encryption and DES; require AES encryption types.

data.name: Tech_T1110_Desc
data.value: Accounts that do not require a password, or whose passwords never expire, weaken resistance to guessing and reuse attacks.

data.name: Tech_T1110_Mit
data.value: Require passwords on all accounts and limit non-expiring passwords to hardened service accounts.

data.name: Tech_T1078.002_Desc
data.value: Highly privileged group membership expands the blast radius of any compromised credential.

data.name: Tech_T1078.002_Mit
data.value: Minimise and regularly review membership of privileged groups; apply tiered administration.

data.name: Tech_T1550_Desc
data.value: Unconstrained delegation lets a compromised host impersonate any user that authenticates to it, enabling credential theft and lateral movement.

data.name: Tech_T1550_Mit
data.value: Remove unconstrained delegation from computers and users (except domain controllers); use constrained or resource-based constrained delegation.

data.name: Tech_T1098_Desc
data.value: Stale, orphaned, or unmanaged accounts (no manager, never logged in, deprovisioned but present) provide durable footholds that evade routine review.

data.name: Tech_T1098_Mit
data.value: Enforce ownership and lifecycle management; disable and remove dormant accounts promptly.

data.name: Tech_T1136_Desc
data.value: Accounts left in a deprovisioned or long-inactive state can be silently reactivated (or their residue reused) to establish persistent access that bypasses normal joiner controls.

data.name: Tech_T1136_Mit
data.value: Complete the deprovisioning lifecycle by disabling and removing dormant accounts; alert on reactivation of previously deprovisioned or stale accounts.

data.name: Tech_T1550.003_Desc
data.value: Service accounts with SPNs and accounts trusted for delegation expand the opportunities to forge or reuse Kerberos tickets (including Silver Tickets) for lateral movement.

data.name: Tech_T1550.003_Mit
data.value: Reduce SPN-bearing user accounts (prefer gMSA), remove unnecessary delegation, and rotate service-account keys regularly.

data.name: Tech_T1484.001_Desc
data.value: Membership in powerful legacy operator groups (Account, Server, Backup Operators) grants directory- or DC-level capabilities that can be abused to modify policy, sign in to controllers, or restore/read protected data.

data.name: Tech_T1484.001_Mit
data.value: Keep legacy operator groups empty and delegate specific, least-privilege permissions instead; monitor membership changes.

data.name: Tech_T1078_Desc
data.value: Expired or locked accounts that remain enabled create inconsistent state that can mask malicious re-use.

data.name: Tech_T1078_Mit
data.value: Reconcile expired and locked accounts; disable rather than leave in an ambiguous state.

data.name: Tech_T1069_Desc
data.value: Empty or unowned groups clutter the directory and complicate the review of effective access an attacker can enumerate.

data.name: Tech_T1069_Mit
data.value: Assign owners to all groups and remove empty groups to keep group scope auditable.

data.name: Tech_T1114_Desc
data.value: Mailbox delegation grants one principal access to another user's mailbox. Full Access exposes another user's mail contents for reading/exfiltration, while Send As and Send on Behalf let a principal send mail as (or on behalf of) another identity - enabling impersonation, spoofing, and business email compromise. Broad or unreviewed delegation widens the mail attack surface.

data.name: Tech_T1114_Mit
data.value: Review mailbox delegation regularly and grant it least-privilege; remove standing Full Access, Send As, and Send on Behalf rights that are not required; prefer shared mailboxes with governed membership over per-user delegation and alert on delegation changes to high-value mailboxes.
